catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-nerin:
An entry on Charles Nerinckx, the Belgian missionary priest called the Apostle of Kentucky and founder of the Sisters of Loretto. Born at Herffelingen in 1761, the eldest of fourteen children, he studied at Louvain and Mechlin, was ordained in 1785, and worked among labourers at Mechlin cathedral. Hunted by the French Directoire for his ministry, he hid for four years at Dendermonde hospital before sailing to America in 1804.

Bishop Carroll assigned him to Kentucky in 1805, a district over two hundred miles long covering nearly half the state. Nerinckx lived in the saddle, founding a congregation or building a church in nearly every year of his mission. He refused the bishopric of New Orleans and crossed the Atlantic twice to recruit helpers. In 1812 he founded the Sisters of Loretto at the Foot of the Cross to secure Catholic schooling for children. He died at Ste. Genevieve, Missouri, in 1824.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-peter-hubert-:
Evermode Backx was the second founder of Tongerloo Abbey in Belgium, born at Tilburg in 1805 and ordained in 1832. Tongerloo, founded in 1128 soon after St. Norbert's order, had once planned to carry on the Bollandists' Acta Sanctorum, but the French Republic expelled its 125 religious in 1796, seized the abbey, and pulled its church down. Belgian independence in 1830 finally let survivors regroup, though only sixteen remained.

Backx's first task was repair: patching what stood, raising new buildings, and buying back the second half of the estate in 1849. In 1852 the papal nuncio laid the first stone of a great new church, and the abbey regained the look of a large, ordered monastery. After twenty-eight years of strenuous rule he died in 1868, regretted by his spiritual children, and successors carried Tongerloo to missions in England and the Congo.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pierre-jean-b:
Pierre-Jean Beckx was a Belgian Jesuit who led the Society of Jesus as its twenty-second superior general. He was born at Sichem in 1795 and ordained in 1819. He worked in Germany and Austria, won converts at Köthen, and served as provincial of Austria. He was elected general in 1853 after the death of Father Roothaan, and held the post for thirty-four years.

Under Beckx the order doubled in size. It opened new provinces in Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, and America. It started missions around the world, even as governments expelled the Jesuits from Italy, Spain, Germany, and France in turn. He retired to Rome in 1883 and died there in 1887.
